title: Jump Game IV
summary: Given an array of integers arr, start at the first index.
statement: Given an array of integers arr, start at the first index. In one step, you can jump to i+1, i-1, or any index j where arr[i] equals arr[j] and i is not equal to j. Find the minimum steps to reach the last index without leaving the array bounds.
constraints: Start at index zero and target the final index.
One move goes to an adjacent index or any other index containing the same value.
Return the minimum number of moves; the one-element array requires zero.
hints: Group all indices by value before searching.
Breadth-first search indices from zero using adjacent and equal-value neighbors.
After expanding one value group, remove it so the same large group is never scanned again.
BFS guarantees the first arrival at the last index is shortest, and clearing a group is safe after its earliest expansion.
editorial: Build a value-to-indices map, then BFS over indices. Adjacent edges and all equal-value edges each cost one. Once the first index of a value is expanded, all positions in that value group receive their earliest possible offers, so deleting the group prevents quadratic rescans. The oracle retains every group and scans all indices on short inputs.

tests.explanation: Jump from zero to equal value at four, step to three, then jump to the final equal 404 in three moves.
The starting index is already the last index.
